blocks.x: Data & Lakehouse in Life & Annuities targets a specific gap: systems exist, but no governed path connects them, which is why surrender and service queues still costs what it costs. The build closes it: we make the source systems agree: one governed definition per metric, streaming where the decision is time-critical, batch where it is not. Life & Annuities is where this discipline pays.

First, the ground Data & Lakehouse work stands on in Life & Annuities: Life books run on decades-long promises: underwriting quality at issue, servicing responsiveness across 30-year relationships, and actuarial integrity across regime changes (IFRS 17/LDTI). The machinery deciding those outcomes is data and document heavy, ideal ground for governed automation.

The fix for surrender and service queues is rarely another screen. It is a governed path between the systems that already exist, instrumented, bounded, and owned by someone with the authority to change the process.

items: Surrender, loan and beneficiary transactions route through document-heavy queues with abandonment risk.

APS records, paramedical data and financial underwriting arrive as documents; assembly consumes days per case.

blocks.x: The first two weeks belong to the baseline. surrender and service queues gets a number, an owner and a signature; the quarter belongs to a bounded slice, Actuarial data workbench, live on your estate. Nothing scales on a demo. The gate criteria are written with your team, and the pilot runs on your data before any rollout plan exists.

Two regimes anchor the Data & Lakehouse frame in Life & Annuities: IFRS 17 / LDTI, actuarial data and reporting discipline; GLBA/privacy regimes, health and financial data duties. The control posture is part of the architecture, which is what makes the audit routine instead of a crisis.
